t2.thesis: A profitable, cash-rich, heavily shorted grower with a strong record of beating estimates gets a small upward tilt from short-covering and its print history, mostly offset by a 16% one-month run-up into the print, management departures and decelerating bookings guidance.
reasons: Last 4 BMO prints: 3 of 4 opened up 18-24%, with consistent EPS beats (6.7-32% surprises).
About 19% of the float is sold short, so a clean beat could trigger a gap up from short-covering.
Q2 margins were already 36.4% adjusted EBITDA and FCF guidance was raised, so the bar is beatable; the consensus range of 0.43-0.67 is wide.
The stock is up 15.8% in one month and 4.4% in 5 days into the print, which raises expectations; ATM IV is 2.35x realized volatility.
The President and EVP Aviation both departed in Sept-Oct, and Q3 bookings guidance implies deceleration to about 20% from 33%.
t2.deciding_variable: Q4 guidance on Total Bookings and revenue, plus Active CLEAR+ member growth and retention, relative to the elevated expectations built up by the October run-up.

The May 2026 print shows a large beat can still open flat or down.
